headline_marked: [[SSC & equivalent exam results]] to be published tomorrow, August 10, at 10 AM
headline: SSC & equivalent exam results to be published tomorrow, August 10, at 10 AM
summary: Students can access their results simultaneously via education board websites, SMS, and their respective institutions. This year's exams saw over 1.85 million candidates participate across 11 boards.
details: The results for this year's SSC and equivalent examinations are scheduled for publication tomorrow, August 10, at 10 AM. Students will be able to access their results simultaneously through education board websites, SMS services, and their respective educational institutions.

To check results online, candidates should visit educationboardresults.gov.bd. They need to select SSC/Dakhil, the exam year, their specific board, and then accurately enter their roll and registration numbers, completing a security captcha before submitting.

For SMS-based results, students can type SSC <Board Name (first 3 letters)> <Roll Number> <Exam Year> and send it to 16140. For example, to get Dhaka Board results, one would send "SSC Dha 123456 [Exam Year]" to 16140.

Madrasa students can pre-register by sending Dakhil <Board Name (first 3 letters)> <Roll> <Exam Year> to 16222. Similarly, technical board students can send SSC TEC <Roll> <Exam Year> to 16222. Pre-registered candidates will automatically receive their results via SMS as soon as they are published.

Educational institutions can obtain institution-specific result sheets by logging into the education board websites (https://eduboardresults.gov.bd and https://educationboardresults.gov.bd) and entering their EIIN in the result corner. It is important to note that results will not be available at education boards, the Ministry of Education, or newspaper offices.

This year's SSC and equivalent theoretical examinations were conducted from April 21 to May 20, followed by practical exams from June 7 to June 14. A total of 1,857,344 candidates, comprising 930,305 males and 927,039 females, participated across 11 education boards.

headline_marked: [[PM Tareque Rahman arrives in Matarbari, Cox's Bazar]] for day-long visit to inspect port, meet flood victims
headline: PM Tareque Rahman arrives in Matarbari, Cox's Bazar for day-long visit to inspect port, meet flood victims
summary: Prime Minister Tareque Rahman is on a day-long tour of Cox's Bazar and Chattogram, focusing on inspecting the Matarbari port and rehabilitating recent flood victims.
details: Prime Minister Tareque Rahman arrived in Matarbari, Cox's Bazar, by an air force helicopter around 10:45 AM on Sunday (August 9). He was welcomed by Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and local leaders upon his arrival.

During his day-long tour, the Prime Minister is scheduled to participate in multiple programs across Maheshkhali, Cox's Bazar, and various areas of Chattogram. A key focus of his visit is the rehabilitation of recent flood victims.

The Prime Minister is set to attend a rehabilitation program for flood-affected individuals at Paschim Banshkhali High School and College field in Baharchhara Union. Later in the afternoon, he will proceed to Fatikchhari Upazila.

From Fatikchhari, Prime Minister Tareque Rahman will visit the Al-Jamiatul Islamia Azizul Ulum Babunagar Madrasa. There, he will pay respects by visiting the grave of the late Allama Shah Ahmad Shafi.

In the evening, the Prime Minister is expected to join another rehabilitation event for flood victims at Hathazari Government College field. He will also participate in an organizational meeting at the Radisson Blu Hotel auditorium in Chattogram.
